column2: An agent should know the price of a job before it asks you to pay. This is Going Rate, for Kite Passport.

Here's a real job: a five-second product video. The agent asks Kite with the caps from the docs example: one dollar a payment. But the video costs a dollar thirty-three. So Kite refuses the first payment, and the agent has to stop and ask you again.

Going Rate checks before the agent asks. Serv Reasoning classifies the job as video generation, and explains the card in one sentence. Plain code computes the going rate: video jobs usually get about three dollars a payment. So this ask is low.
The going rate goes into Kite's task summary, so you see it on Kite's own approval screen, right where you tap your passkey.
Same job, with Going Rate's caps. One passkey approval, and the first paid call goes through. Here's the transaction, on Base.
Every real payment is on the ledger: five task types, with the listed price next to what Kite actually charged. Listed prices were off by up to eighty percent.
Going Rate. The going rate of the task, so you approve once.
